result:
Round 357 (PERF-10a) failed, and the next task, round 358, re-dispatches PERF-10a with my ruling on the bug C found. The decision is **CONTINUE**. Gate 357 was skipped, so the baseline stays `d49536b`. I didn't touch `store/`: it still has A's 56 changed files.

**Why it failed.** A stopped on a Medium review finding that I hadn't ruled on, and C reproduced it in a real browser as C-R357-01. On A's tree, resizing below 900 px and back makes the stopped insert-marker status gain an extra "Tempo 120 BPM…" sentence, and the status is not announced again. On HEAD only the insert-marker sentence remains. C didn't run the perf, play, follow, video or narrow-screen checks, so PERF-10a is not done and the status board marks it ბაგია.

**Ruling: restore HEAD's text and order.**
- This round promised no behaviour change. The extra sentence only appears because the tempo seed re-runs on every remount, which is a separate older defect. Accepting the new text would build on that defect.
- The fix changes only `StudioWorkspace.tsx`:
  - The follow component now acts only when playback starts or stops.
  - A new on-mount effect, placed after the tempo-seed effect as on HEAD, writes the status the same way HEAD did.
- I tested the fix on a scratch copy outside `store/`:
  - Two new tests (RM1/RM2) fail on A's tree and pass on HEAD and on the fix. They cover both halves of the bug.
  - Two new mutants turn RM1/RM2 red. The four earlier mutants give exactly the same failures as A's round 357.
  - The 71 affected test files pass (1290/1290), and typecheck and Biome pass.
  - C's own browser probe on the fix matches HEAD on all 7 steps.
- I did not re-run the 8-minute perf spec. The change adds no component or render, and A and C still run it in full.
- Side effect: the scratch dev server rebuilt the shared Vite cache in `node_modules/.vite`. It's only a cache, and the task tells C to restart the :5173 server if it is stale.

**Round 358:**
- **A** keeps its tree and applies only this fix plus the new test file. It also updates doc 234's status line to round 358 and re-runs the code review.
- **C** runs every check skipped in round 357, plus:
  - the C-R357-01 recipe, compared with HEAD;
  - a record-only check on HEAD of whether a typed BPM is lost after the resize;
  - the auth check and the doc check.

**Backlog and status board (backlog v320 → v321, decisions D-29z1155 to D-29z1158):**
- C-R357-01 is open as Medium, fixed by this task.
- Four Lows from A's code review (including the tempo re-seed on remount) are logged as open and deferred to the polish pass.
- The reviewer's Architecture note is recorded as a signal, not scheduled. I've repeated the request for a bounded `frontend-architect` checkpoint from root. It doesn't block PERF-10a.
- The order after this round is unchanged: regression on or after 2026-11-08, then PERF-10a-BUDGETS, PERF-10b and the rest of the queue.
- I parked one lesson idea for RETRO 368 because `lessons.md` is already at 60 lines: when an effect moves into a child component, the task lists the parent's effects that write the same state, in mount order, and includes a remount check.

The advisor was available and consulted twice. Following its review, the mutant expectations now match measured results, A proves the bug by test order on its real tree, and the typed-BPM check runs with the clip still loaded.

- `b-round-357.md`
- `b-next.json`
